content.comment_body: New features for upcoming [product_name] [version_no] ([article_no]) have been announced. Highlights include improved connections to various cloud providers such as Azure and Alibaba, addition of a decimal display format for cloud data, and an extension of the variable memory area with new sections (VX and VR) for both volatile and retentive data, which synchronize with the SD card. The device now supports sending customized emails at specific trigger events once configured in [product_name] [document]. Diagnostics now include an 'Email' menu. Data logging has been enhanced for online viewing and uploading via the web server. A soft keyboard has been added for changing names, passwords, or switching user roles. The online nameplate feature allows scanning a QR code to access device information, ordering, technical documentation, and software updates. Additionally, micro SD card support has been expanded to include exFAT formatted cards alongside FAT32.
As a dedicated user, I'm pleased to see [product_name] is still maintained and under active development by [company_name].

I'm excited about these updates! However, I have a question regarding the new decimal cloud data format: is there any chance this feature could be added to previous [version_no] hardware? I have multiple devices in various locations, and having to work with different data formats would be inconvenient, as the decimal format is more user-friendly than binary.
I hope to see support for SCL programming language added in future updates.
I was hoping for SCL as well! I've often considered seeking outside help to move beyond the limitations of graphical programming environments.
It would be great if future versions of [product_name] allowed direct code access to system date and time areas.

From my perspective: 1) If HMI input is saved immediately to the SD card, it's not possible to restore factory values easily. 2) If HMI input isn't saved to the SD card and the SD card is read on every boot, then entered HMI data is ignored, and each start resets everything to defaults. Is it one of these, or something else?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are enthusiastic about new features for [product_name] [version_no], such as enhanced cloud integration, expanded memory options, and improved data handling. Some users would like these features to be available on earlier models and ask for more advanced programming options like SCL language support and direct access to system date/time from code. There is also a discussion about data consistency between HMI input and SD card values, indicating a desire for clear and flexible data management. Backward compatibility and more programming flexibility remain key user concerns.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect new features, like cloud data format options, to be provided for older hardware when possible, additional programming language support (such as SCL), the ability to access system date and time in user code, and consistent behavior regarding how HMI inputs interact with SD card data.
pain_keywords: unclear data synchronization between HMI and SD card
limited access to system resources from code
